# Set-up

This markdown will generate an empty droplet object that can be used as background for ambient RNA correction tools, such as `soupX` and `decontX`. 

To avoid confusion, please review the following table for commonly used terminology in this markdown"


| Term(s) | Description | 
| :------: | :------: | 
| cell/pseudo-GEM/pseudo_droplet   | We use these terms interchangeably with barcodes. It describes a unique combination of sample and droplet barcode, which ideally would be one single-cell, and corresponds to a GEM in regular single-cell | 
| droplet/GEM| We refer to a droplet/GEM as the combination of all cells that carry the same droplet barcode. These cells were co-captured in GEMs during the sequencing process and are therefore true multiplets that we can re-create   | 
| empty cell | cells/barcodes which are considered empty by both `cellranger multi` and `DropletUtils::emptyDrops()`  | 
| empty droplet | droplets which do not contain any non-empty cells | 

In 10xFlex data, the raw count matrix is presented as cell x gene matrices. In regular droplet based approaches, this is equivalent of saying it represents a droplet x gene matrix. All ambient RNA correction tools were designed under the assumption that each column in the matrix is a *droplet* - however, this assumption is not met in 10x Flex data. There is no general recommendation for whether the background should be provided as empty *droplets* (so cells combined based on their droplet barcode) or empty *cells* (matrix as is). The distribution of ambient RNA in 10xFlex is not fully understood. 

For the purpose of we therefore clarify in detail how we define the background in detail here as well as in the methods.

- determine empty cells using both `cellranger multi` as well as `DropletUtils::emptyDrops()`

- only keep "empty cells" that come from droplets where no cells were called

- Combine resulting "empty cells" into their respective "empty droplets" based on their droplet barcode. *The resulting background object will be in droplet x gene format*



## Load libraries

```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(here)
  library(glue)
  library(DropletUtils)
  library(scran)
  library(scater)
  library(scuttle)
  library(scales)
  library(readr)
  library(Seurat)
  library(scDblFinder)
  library(scMerge)
  library(ggpubr)
  library(BiocParallel)
  library(clustree)
  library(SingleCellExperiment)
  library(scMerge)
  library(Matrix)
  library(SeuratDisk)
  library(qs2)
  library(patchwork)
  library(decontX)
})


```


## Load data

```{r}
#raw output
raw_sce <- read10xCounts(here("data/Tonsils_10xFlex/raw_feature_bc_matrix"), row.names = "symbol", col.names = T)

#cellranger filtered output 
sce <- readRDS(here("data/Tonsils_10xFlex/G000231_Neeland_batch9_Tonsils.CellRanger_filtered.SCE.rds"))
# we really only need the barcodes for this - get those and then clean up
cellranger_barcodes <- colnames(sce)
rm(sce)
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
gc()

```


# Add cell information to empty object

As a first step, we will be adding information on whether or not a barcode is considered a non-empty cell using both `cellranger multi` as well as `DropletUtils::emptyDrops()`. 

## `cellranger multi`

This is the easier step, we can just use all the barcodes detected in the filtered cellranger output matrix.

```{r}
raw_sce$is_cell_cellranger <- ifelse(raw_sce$Barcode %in% cellranger_barcodes, "yes", "no")
raw_sce$is_cell_cellranger %>% table()
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
rm(cellranger_barcodes);gc()

```


## `DropletUtils::emptyDrops()`

```{r}
# follow basic vignette: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc//vignettes/DropletUtils/inst/doc/DropletUtils.html#detecting-empty-droplets
set.seed(100)
e.out <- emptyDrops(counts(raw_sce))
is.cell <- e.out$FDR <= 0.01 
is.cell[is.na(is.cell)] <- FALSE #NAs are not cells
non_emptydrops <- raw_sce$Barcode[is.cell]

#add to raw object
raw_sce$is_cell_emptyDrops <- ifelse(raw_sce$Barcode %in% non_emptydrops, "yes", "no")
raw_sce$is_cell_emptyDrops %>% table()

```


## Compare cell calling for both methods

Simple table to quantify. This is just an overview. 

```{r}
table(raw_sce$is_cell_cellranger,raw_sce$is_cell_emptyDrops , dnn=c("cellranger", "emptyDrops"))
```

Essentially we're interested in the no - no cells. 

Add that information to the object. Only consider cells that are called in both. 

```{r}
raw_sce$is_cell <- ifelse(raw_sce$is_cell_cellranger == "no" & raw_sce$is_cell_emptyDrops == "no", "no", "yes")

raw_sce$is_cell %>% table()
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
rm(e.out, non_emptydrops, is.cell);gc()
```


# Determine droplets with no cells - empty droplets

Next, we will find droplets (based on barcode) for which no non-empty cells were identified. 

```{r}
#add droplet barcode
raw_sce$GEM_barcode <- substring(raw_sce$Barcode, first = 1, last = 17)


filter_GEMs <- table(raw_sce$GEM_barcode, raw_sce$is_cell) %>% as.data.frame() %>%
  pivot_wider(., names_from = "Var2", values_from = "Freq") %>%
  dplyr::rename(Barcode=Var1, empty_count=no, cell_count=yes) %>% 
  mutate(., select = ifelse(cell_count == 0, T, F)) %>%
  filter(., select == T)  #select the ones with no cell count 

knitr::kable(head(filter_GEMs)) 

```


# create empty cells only object

Finally, lets subset to generate this new, empty cells only object. 

```{r}
raw_sce_subset <- raw_sce[, raw_sce$GEM_barcode %in% filter_GEMs$Barcode]
raw_sce_subset
```

# create empty *droplets* object

Only keep cells that are considered empty by both cellranger multi as well as `DropletUtils::emptyDrops()`, then only keep empty cells that come from droplets with no cells in them. Re-combine into empty droplets using George’s function.

```{r}
# function written by George Howitt
makeGEMMatrix <- function(sce) {
  counts_matrix <- counts(sce)
  dimnames(counts_matrix)[[2]] <- substring(dimnames(counts_matrix)[[2]], first = 1, last = 17) #first 17 bases are droplet barcodes
  counts_matrix <- as(counts_matrix, "TsparseMatrix")
  nms <- colnames(counts_matrix)
  uniquenms <- unique(nms)
  GEM_counts <- sparseMatrix(i = counts_matrix@i+1,
                             j = match(nms, uniquenms)[counts_matrix@j + 1],
                             x = counts_matrix@x,
                             dimnames = list(rownames(counts_matrix), uniquenms),
                             repr = 'T')
  return(as(GEM_counts, "CsparseMatrix"))
}
```


```{r}
# make sure to remove genes with no expression across the board as this breaks the function
empty_droplet <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(counts=makeGEMMatrix(raw_sce_subset[rowSums(counts(raw_sce_subset)) > 0,])))
empty_droplet
```


```{r, include=FALSE}
#hidden clean up 
rm(raw_sce_subset);gc()
```



## Look at summary metrics

Let's look at summary metrics for this set of empty cells 

```{r}
is.mito <- grepl(pattern = "^MT", rownames(empty_droplet))
empty_droplet <- addPerCellQCMetrics(empty_droplet, subsets = list(mito = is.mito))
```

```{r}
df_summary_cells <- empty_droplet@colData %>% as.data.frame() %>% 
  select(., c("sum", "detected", "subsets_mito_detected")) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols=c("sum", "detected", "subsets_mito_detected"), names_to = "metric", values_to = "entry") %>% 
  group_by(metric) %>% 
  summarise(., 
            min=min(entry), 
            q25 = quantile(entry, 0.25),
            mean = mean(entry), 
            median =median(entry),
            q75 = quantile(entry, 0.75),
            q90=quantile(entry, 0.9),
            max = max(entry)
            ) 


knitr::kable(df_summary_cells)
  
```




How many empty cells have a library count > 1000?

```{r}
#absolute number
sum(empty_droplet$sum > 1000)

#proportion
sum(empty_droplet$sum > 1000)/ncol(empty_droplet)

```

A very small proportion of empty cells has a weirdly high library size. However, as it is a very small fraction (~0.1%), this should be okay. 


## export 

Let's export the empty object!

```{r}
filename <- here("output/data/Tonsils_10xFlex/Engineered/Tonsils_10xFlex_engineered_emptyObject")

DropletUtils::write10xCounts(path = filename,
                             x = counts(empty_droplet),
                             version = "3", 
                             overwrite = T)

```
